## Learning objectives

By the end of this session you will:

- Compute and interpret **descriptive statistics** (mean, median, sd, etc.) in R.
- Understand **distributions** and basic **hypothesis testing** (e.g. t-test, chi-squared).
- Fit and interpret **linear models** (`lm()`) for continuous outcomes.
- Use **model output** (coefficients, R², p-values) in a linguistic context.
- Reference **Winter (2020)** or similar for statistics for linguists.

# Descriptive statistics

- **Measures of central tendency**: mean, median.
- **Spread**: standard deviation, variance, range, IQR.
- **By group**: e.g. `group_by()` + `summarize()` with `mean()`, `sd()`, `n()`.

*[Add code chunks using a dataset from the course, e.g. reaction times, word frequencies, or population.]*

# Distributions and exploratory checks

- **Distributions**: normal, skewed; histograms and density plots.
- **Assumptions**: when parametric tests are appropriate.

*[Add brief code or references to visualization (Session 4) and to Winter/textbook.]*

# Hypothesis testing

- **t-test** — comparing means (e.g. two groups).
- **Chi-squared test** — categorical data (e.g. contingency tables).
- **Interpretation**: p-values, effect size, confidence intervals.

*[Add code: `t.test()`, `chisq.test()`, and interpretation.]*

# Linear models

- **`lm()`** — formula interface (e.g. `y ~ x`, `y ~ x1 + x2`).
- **Categorical predictors**: treatment coding; interpreting coefficients.
- **Model output**: `summary()`, coefficients, R², F-test.

*[Add one or two examples relevant to language data.]*

# Hands-on exercises

- Compute descriptive statistics by group and interpret.
- Run a t-test or chi-squared test and report results.
- Fit a simple linear model and interpret coefficients.

# Summary and further reading

- Winter, B. [Statistics for linguists](https://appliedstatisticsforlinguists.org/) (R introduction).
- R4DS [Model basics](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/model-basics.html) (optional).
- [Lin611 — Quantitative Methods in Linguistics](https://jofrhwld.github.io/2023_Lin611/).
